result.topic_en: Riemann derives from the normal-coordinate conditions at a point O that the first derivatives of the metric coefficients vanish and the second derivatives satisfy symmetry relations, and expresses the line element near O as $ds_0^2$ plus a quadrilinear curvature term (equation 8).
result.transcription:
Hinc posito $t_{\iota\iota'} = p_{\iota,\iota,\iota'}$ [?]

$p_{\iota\iota'\iota''} = 0$ ; $\frac{\partial p_{\iota\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial p_{\iota\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial p_{\iota\iota'''\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}} = 0$ in puncto O

E quarum prima sequitur, addendo $p_{\iota'\iota\iota''} = 0$ :

(5.) $\frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}} = 0$ in puncto o

E secunda:

$2\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}}\right) = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'''\iota'}}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'''}}$

Hinc permutando $\iota$ et $\iota'$ et addendo, si denotamus
per S summam omnium sex derivationum secundi ordinis
[-gradus-] formae $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}$ :

$S = 3\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} - \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)$

Et quum S non mutetur, mutatis $\iota''\iota'''$ [-etiam-] cum $\iota\iota'$

6. $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}$

7. $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'''\iota'}}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota'''}} = 0$ } in puncto O.

Nunc est quadratum elementi linearis a puncto o
ducti

$ds_0^2 = \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$ ,

a puncto $dx_1 \ldots dx_n$ ducti, puncto O infinite vicino:

$ds^2 = \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''} \left(\frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}}\right)_0 \delta x_{\iota''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''} \left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 \delta x_{\iota''}\delta x_{\iota'''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$

In parte dextra hujus expressionis terminus secundus
evanescit ope aequationis 5. Terminus tertius ita
exhiberi potest:

$dd\sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} = \delta\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$

si quidem variationes [-d et $\delta$ independentes supponuntur-] secundi ordinis $ddx_\iota$ $d\delta x_\iota$ $\delta\delta x_\iota$ evanescunt.
At facile deducitur ex aequatione (7):

$dd\sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} + 2 d\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} = 0$

unde hic terminus fit:

$dd\sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'}\delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} = \frac{1}{3}\{dd\sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'}\delta x_\iota\delta x_{\iota'} - 2 d\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} + \delta\delta\sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}\}$

qui et ipse facile in formam redit:

$\frac{4}{3}\sum_{\iota\iota'',\iota'\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'}\delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$

si summa ad diversa tantum paria indicum $\iota\iota''$ et ad
diversa tantum paria indicum $\iota'\iota'''$ extenditur; unde
denique:

8. $ds^2 = ds_0^2 + \frac{2}{3}\sum_{\iota\iota'',\iota'\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota\delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'}\delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$

Jam si {+in+} locos variabilium $x$ quaelibet aliae introducuntur,
conditiones hujus expressionis non erunt eaedem, neque
erunt verae aequationes 4. 5. 6, neque evanescent variatio-
nes secundi [-gradus-] {+ordinis+} $dd$, $d\delta$, $\delta\delta$. Hae conditiones itaque

[margin: subsistent [?] / vigebunt [?]] [margin: NB.]

methods.what: Vanishing of first derivatives of metric coefficients at origin of normal coordinates
Pair-exchange symmetry of second derivatives of metric at O
methods.quote: 6. $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}$

methods.what: Cyclic (Bianchi-type) identity for second derivatives of metric at O
methods.quote: 7. $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'''\iota'}}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota'''}} = 0$ } in puncto O.

methods.what: Sum S of the six second derivatives expressed via symmetrization
methods.quote: $S = 3\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_{\iota'}} - \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)$

methods.what: Second-order Taylor expansion of line element near O
methods.quote: $ds^2 = \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''} \left(\frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}}\right)_0 \delta x_{\iota''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''} \left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 \delta x_{\iota''}\delta x_{\iota'''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$

methods.what: Relation between second variations derived from equation 7
methods.quote: $dd\sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} + 2 d\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} = 0$

methods.what: Line element near O as ds_0^2 plus quadrilinear curvature form in bivectors (Riemann curvature expression)
methods.quote: 8. $ds^2 = ds_0^2 + \frac{2}{3}\sum_{\iota\iota'',\iota'\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota\delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'}\delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$

items.quote:
Jam si {+in+} locos variabilium $x$ quaelibet aliae introducuntur,
conditiones hujus expressionis non erunt eaedem, neque
erunt verae aequationes 4. 5. 6, neque evanescent variatio-
nes secundi [-gradus-] {+ordinis+} $dd$, $d\delta$, $\delta\delta$.
items.english: Now if any other variables are introduced in place of the variables x, the conditions of this expression will not be the same, nor will equations 4, 5, 6 be true, nor will the second-order variations dd, dδ, δδ vanish.
